title: Fuel Accounting Basis Note — Pricing a Gallon on a Refined Fuels and Propane Account
content:
What a gallon costs is fixed by the programme's price basis and by whether contracted gallons remain, and it is never negotiated on the truck.

**Posted-price programmes.** The clause formerly stated here — "Where the programme prices at the posted price, the price is the day's rack for the product plus the programme's margin, taken on the day the fuel was pumped and not the day the invoice was cut." — is carried for the record and is no longer in force as the basis on which a posted price is arrived at. It is superseded by the current basis for arriving at the posted price on an account under Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts, and the desk works from that current basis rather than from the sentence above.

**Contracted-price programmes.** Where the programme prices at the contracted price, gallons draw at the booked price until the booking is exhausted and at the posted price afterwards, and the two are shown as separate rows on the same ticket so that a part-contracted fill is never averaged into one price.

**Which booking is drawn.** Contracted gallons are drawn oldest booking first and only against the product and the account they were booked on.

**Automatic fills.** Where the tank is filled on a keep-full schedule and a booking exists, the booking is drawn automatically without the member having to ask.

**The money on a ticket.** The money a row on the ticket comes to is the gallons on that row multiplied by the price per gallon for that row, rounded to two decimal places.

**A query on a stop already billed.** A member who believes they should have been charged the contracted price on a stop already billed is answered from the booking record and the ticket, and where the booking was genuinely exhausted the posted price stands.

## Worked illustration (hypothetical inputs)

A member on a contracted-price programme holds 200.0 gallons still standing to their credit at a booked price of 1.7500 USD per gallon, and takes a fill of 320.0 gallons on a day whose posted price is 2.1000 USD per gallon. The booked gallons are exhausted first, so 200.0 gallons draw at the booked price and the remaining 120.0 gallons draw at the posted price. The ticket carries two rows: 200.0 gallons at 1.7500 USD per gallon, coming to 350.00 USD, and 120.0 gallons at 2.1000 USD per gallon, coming to 252.00 USD. The two are never averaged into a single price per gallon on the ticket.

Had that member held two bookings, the older of the two would have been drawn down first, and only against the same fuel on the same account.

superseded_clauses: Where the programme prices at the posted price, the price is the day's rack for the product plus the programme's margin, taken on the day the fuel was pumped and not the day the invoice was cut.
